statement: Crypto choices rest on current primary standards (RFC 8452, 9771, 5869, 2104/4231, 7748, 9106, 8032, 3161/5816; FIPS 180-4, FIPS 203, SP 800-227; X-Wing draft 10) plus the CCS 2025 CDC and USENIX 2022 key-commitment papers, not legacy archive precedent.

Candidates were judged on standardized meaning, misuse behavior, cryptanalytic history, implementation/interoperability availability, hardware dependence, bounded resources, license, and long-term decodability; a second pass treated the frozen draft as hostile, seeking ambiguity, downgrade, replay, nonce, resource, and lifecycle gaps.
evidence_in_source: internal review narrative; no external reviewer named
research_needed: Independent external cryptographic review repeating the hostile pass

statement: Suite-1 payload AEAD is AES-256-GCM-SIV (RFC 8452): fixed 32-byte key, 12-byte nonce, 16-byte tag, published vectors, nonce-misuse resistance, independent implementations; can use AES acceleration yet remains portably implementable.
research_needed: Benchmark GCM-SIV throughput on CPUs without AES acceleration (portable fallback) at archive scale

statement: A two-pass (SIV) encryptor is acceptable for archive records because Entrybound already has bounded, independently framed physical objects.
research_needed: Measure encrypt throughput and peak buffering of two-pass GCM-SIV at the 64 MiB maximum payload record

statement: Nonce-misuse resistance is not relied upon: Entrybound still uses random segment salts, derived keys, structured nonces, and rejects repeated segment ordinals.
research_needed: Property test that no two generated records share (key, nonce)

statement: Readers must not release plaintext before AEAD tag confirmation, per RFC 8452; this matches Entrybound's required reader architecture.
evidence_in_source: primary citation (RFC 8452); implementation note L167-171 states extraction only after full verification
research_needed: Fault-injection test that no plaintext reaches output, callbacks, or temp files before tag verification

location: §Payload AEAD comparison > Rejected payload candidates L76

research_needed: Performance comparison on hardware lacking AES acceleration (where ChaCha usually wins)

location: §Payload AEAD comparison > Rejected payload candidates L77

statement: The design avoids any mutable cross-process nonce state.

Key/nonce uniqueness: a fresh archive ID enters root extraction; independent class roots separate control and payload; each segment has a random salt and globally unique ordinal; nonce prefixes separate DATA from END. A repeated 16-byte salt cannot repeat a key when class or ordinal differs.
research_needed: Formal or property-based proof that (key, nonce) pairs never repeat across classes, segments, and END records

statement: Duplicate segment ordinals are rejected before decrypting.
Segment limits: at most 2^20-1 DATA messages, 1 GiB private data, and 64 MiB maximum payload record, far below primitive maxima, to bound counters, buffering, and failure scope.
evidence_in_source: none (no measurement cited for chosen values)
research_needed: Benchmark memory, throughput, and corruption blast radius at these limits; check interaction with large solid Chunks/ChunkGroups and planner outputs

statement: SegmentEnd binds the ordered record headers and ciphertexts of its segment.

A terminal ArchiveFinal binds prior completed segments, resources, identities, recipient set, Descriptor/manifest objects, and the intended footer, covering reordering, truncation, and splicing without an external mutable global nonce counter.
research_needed: Negative tests for reorder/truncate/splice across segments and archives

statement: Absolute offsets are not AEAD associated data for bulk records, so an envelope-size change can move ciphertext without re-encryption; offsets are validated through the authenticated FooterCore bound in ArchiveFinal.

Exact segment and record headers are AD; the review checked that no unauthenticated field can change accepted meaning, and a pre-authentication locator edit causes at worst bounded parsing work or failure.
research_needed: Field-by-field formal audit plus fuzzing of public framing; measure worst-case pre-authentication work

statement: In encrypted archives only crypto discovery, recipient discovery, and minimal ciphertext framing are public.
Under the new required crypto feature, the old preamble budget fields become zero sentinels; real resource budgets are encrypted.
refines_or_supersedes: Changes public preamble budget-field semantics defined by the container spec (ECF preamble)

statement: Encrypting budgets and control data avoids leaking entry count, logical size, names, manifests, Index, codec choices, identity roots, and signers.
research_needed: Leakage analysis of all public bytes including section sizes, segment counts, record counts and padded lengths as indirect signals

statement: Encrypted STREAM is rejected for crypto v1 because STREAM places content before its manifest; v1 fails before output rather than secretly buffering, silently changing layout, or leaking the manifest, retaining one confidentiality contract.

Encrypted STREAM with equivalent name/metadata privacy and final authentication would need staging or new ordering semantics; stdin/stdout encryption would materially change secure error recovery and key-envelope updates. Not designed for v1.
research_needed: Design study of an encrypted sequential layout (bounded staging, trailer manifest) and its privacy/recovery properties
decision_needed: Should a later crypto version define encrypted STREAM or pipe encryption, and under what privacy contract?

No classical-only public-key recipient creator is included, avoiding a switch that could accidentally weaken hybrid confidentiality.
evidence_in_source: design statement; implementation notes list classical-only recipients as unimplemented

statement: Password mode is kept separate from public-key recipients because its security is governed by human entropy.
Password KDF is Argon2id version 19 for memory hardness, hybrid data-independent/dependent behavior, standard encoding semantics, and broad maintained implementations.

PBKDF2 rejected for cheap GPU/ASIC parallelism; scrypt credible but Argon2id has the more current standard and explicit parameters; Argon2d alone has weaker side-channel resistance; Argon2i alone needs more passes.
Default password creation profile is 256 MiB memory, three passes, four lanes, aimed at infrequent offline archives rather than high-throughput login servers.
research_needed: Measure unlock latency and memory feasibility on low-end, 32-bit, mobile and WASM targets; compare with RFC 9106 recommended profiles
decision_needed: Should the CLI offer alternative password cost profiles, and what caller default maxima apply when reading?

statement: Wire bounds prevent a malicious archive from demanding arbitrary Argon2 resources, and caller maxima may be lower than wire bounds.
Argon2id uses raw password bytes and raw-hash APIs, avoiding PHC-string parsing and normalization ambiguity.
research_needed: Cross-platform unlock tests with non-ASCII passwords (NFC vs NFD input, Windows console code pages, terminal encodings)
decision_needed: Should the CLI normalize typed passwords (e.g. Unicode NFC) before raw-byte hashing so the same password unlocks on every OS?

statement: Residual risk: the public commitment and wrapped-key tag make offline password guesses testable; the design does not claim to remove this oracle.
research_needed: Estimate attacker guess cost at default Argon2id parameters on GPU/ASIC

statement: Password mode cannot borrow the security label of hybrid recipients and cannot be mixed with them in one archive.
Padding uses quarter-octave buckets rather than powers of two, capping proportional overhead below 25% for records above the minimum while coarsening length observations.
research_needed: Quantify residual length leakage and actual overhead on representative corpora

statement: Three padding modes: maximum padding is intentionally expensive and does not hide record count; no padding exposes exact private-record length; all three modes are authenticated and inspectable.
The CCS 2025 keyed-CDC analysis recovers keys from several deployed folklore secret-chunking schemes under weak known/chosen-plaintext conditions.
The default secret Gear table for encrypted chunking is documented only as defense in depth, not as a boundary-privacy guarantee.
research_needed: Evaluate practical boundary-inference attacks against Entrybound's default keyed Gear chunker
decision_needed: Should PHTE strong boundaries become the default for encrypted archives given the default Gear table is known-breakable?

statement: The optional strong boundary mode instantiates the paper's universal-polynomial-hash-then-AES PRF construction with exact field, window, and encoding rules.
The paper measured roughly 53%-165% slowdown from per-byte AES in patched Restic experiments, which supports keeping the strong mode explicit rather than silently imposing it.
research_needed: Measure PHTE chunking cost inside Entrybound with and without AES acceleration

statement: Neither padding nor keyed boundaries provide total traffic-flow or size hiding: the last Chunk, archive total, record count, remote requests, and some within-archive equality remain visible.
research_needed: Characterize remote range-request access-pattern leakage for encrypted INDEXED archives

statement: Signatures use pure Ed25519 for deterministic signing, fixed compact encodings, widely implemented RFC vectors, simple keys, and no per-signature random-nonce failure.
ECDSA P-256 rejected for complex encoding/nonce/malleability handling, RSA-PSS for large keys/signatures, ML-DSA for larger artifacts and newer operational ecosystem.
Record-now-decrypt-later motivates post-quantum encryption but not, today, post-quantum signatures; a future signature algorithm gets a new authenticated algorithm ID and feature.
research_needed: Track ML-DSA/hybrid signature ecosystem maturity for long-lived archive signatures
decision_needed: When should a post-quantum or hybrid signature algorithm be added for long-retention archives?

statement: Signatures cover canonical stored binding values; each is then separately compared to the current archive, distinguishing forgery (INVALID) from a legitimate historical statement whose content, physical organization, or addressing is now STALE.
The addressing binding includes the archive ID so a signature over the same recipient set/commitment cannot be forwarded to a different encryption epoch.

RFC 3161 timestamps are optional and separately statused; v1 limits imprint to SHA-256 and CMS signer to Ed25519 to avoid an archive-controlled PKI algorithm list; no network fetch is required or performed.
research_needed: Survey whether real public/commercial RFC 3161 TSAs issue Ed25519-signed tokens; if few or none, the feature is practically unusable
decision_needed: Should the timestamp profile admit RSA/ECDSA TSA signers to interoperate with deployed TSAs?

statement: Crate versions are exact intended pins; project MSRV is Rust 1.94 and all selected primitive crates declare MSRV 1.89 or lower, so no MSRV increase is required.
